About this role: The NPI Engineering Manager leads the New Product Introduction engineering team responsible for bringing new and transferred products into serial production. This role owns industrialization, process and product validation, and launch readiness from early design input through pilot builds, first-of-kind production, start of production and rate ramp. The manager is accountable for delivering assigned programs on time, at target cost, at required quality and at committed capacity, and for the readiness evidence leadership relies on to authorize production. The role leads a team of NPI engineers, project engineers and technicians, and works daily with Design Engineering, Program Management, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Operations, Finance and EH&S. Scope includes new production lines and line conversions, tooling and equipment, capital execution, workstation and material-presentation design, standard work and operator training, and the handoff into sustaining operations. Performance is measured by launch and gate adherence, first-pass yield and defects per unit at launch, supplier and material readiness to clear-to-build, unit cost and labor hours against plan, capital spend against approved budget, and line rate achieved against designed rate. Key Responsibilities: Leads, staffs and develops the NPI engineering team, setting priorities, workload balance, decision rights and escalation triggers across concurrent programs. Owns manufacturing and launch readiness for assigned programs from design input through pilot, first-of-kind build, start of production and rate ramp. Represents Operations in phase-gate and design reviews, presenting readiness status, risk, and the evidence required to authorize production. Owns APQP, PFMEA, control plan, PPAP and process-validation execution, and drives design-for-manufacturability input before design freeze. Directs industrialization of new lines and line conversions: process flow, layout, takt and line balance, labor models, tooling, fixtures, equipment and run-test capability. Plans and executes capital and tooling projects, including justification, specification, supplier selection, installation, commissioning and run-off to qualified rate. Manages program budgets, engineering resources, schedules and risk-mitigation plans, and escalates constraints with options and a recommendation. Drives material and supplier readiness with Supply Chain and Quality, including BOM accuracy, PPAP completion, first-article approval and clear-to-build status. Coordinates pilot runs, validation builds and production transfer with cross-functional teams, closing known-not-perfect issues and build-quality findings before ramp. Establishes routings, standard work, work instructions, operator training and certification requirements, and ergonomic and job-hazard reviews for new processes. Governs engineering change during launch, ensuring configuration control and disciplined implementation into production. Executes formal handoff to sustaining Manufacturing Engineering, Quality and Operations, with defined acceptance criteria and post-launch performance follow-up. Coaches and develops NPI engineers and technicians through skills matrices, structured problem solving and succession planning. Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree and 8+ years of New Product Introduction, manufacturing engineering, industrialization or product-launch experience in a manufacturing environment or Master’s degree and 6+ years of New Product Introduction, manufacturing engineering, industrialization or product-launch experience in a manufacturing environment 3+ years leading engineering teams, either as direct reports or as the accountable leader of matrixed project teams. 5+ years applying APQP, PFMEA, control plans, PPAP and process validation on production launches. 3+ years managing launches to defined time, cost, quality and capacity gates, including pilot builds, start of production and rate ramp. Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechatronics or Electrical Engineering. 3+ years in HVAC, refrigeration, or comparable large-format discrete assembly involving sheet metal fabrication, welding or brazing, piping, and electrical build-up. Experience standing up new production lines or a new site, including layout, takt and labor modeling, equipment installation and ramp to qualified rate. 2+ years leading NPI or industrialization across multiple sites or in a cross-border US and Mexico manufacturing network; conversational Spanish a plus. 3+ years managing project budgets and engineering resources, including capital or tooling projects of $1M or greater from business case through installation, qualification and spend tracking against approved budget. PMP, Six Sigma Black Belt, or Green Belt combined with a recognized Lean certification. Working proficiency with SAP or equivalent ERP, PLM such as Windchill, CAD such as Creo or SolidWorks, MES, and project tools such as Asana, Smartsheet or MS Project. Experience with product certification and code requirements such as UL or ETL listing, ASME pressure-vessel scope, and run-test or performance-validation methods. Demonstrated development of engineers and technicians, including skills matrices, certification plans and promotion of team members into expanded roles. jobs.description: Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads. Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience. As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people. We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you! Are you passionate about building intelligent systems that personalize experiences for hundreds of millions of customers? Do you want to work at the intersection of deep learning, causal inference, and product optimization, where your models directly shape how customers experience advertising on one of the world’s largest streaming platforms? Prime Video Ads is redefining what ad-supported streaming looks like. We launched ads on Prime Video in 2024 and are now in the process of building the science foundation to make our ad experience the most customer-centric in the industry. Unlike traditional digital advertising where clicks and conversions provide direct feedback, streaming presents unique scientific challenges. Indirect signals, heterogeneous customer responses, and the need to balance monetization with long-term engagement, all at massive scale. Key job responsibilities The Science Our team tackles problems that span the full ML lifecycle, from exploratory research and offline modeling to online experimentation and production deployment. The science challenges include: * Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time. * Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals. * Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles. * Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies. * Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric. A day in the life * Lead the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind * Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale * Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements * Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions * Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions About the team The PV Ad CX team’s mission is to create the world’s most customer-centric ad experience for video streaming. We build adaptive systems that determine when, how many, and what ads to show each customer, personalized to their viewing behavior, content context, and engagement patterns. We aspire to transform ad breaks from interruptions into moments that feel relevant and thoughtful.

Drive vendor and in-house parts from concept to qualified production, including sheet metal, extrusions, busbar, manifolds, cable management, and rack accessories
Stand on the floor during prototype and production builds: debug fit, leak, cable dress, airflow/liquid balance, and service time; fold issues into the next revision the same day

Experience or background in ethernet switching, networking, interconnects, and high power distribution

Cable and fiber physical design inside the rack (MPO/OSFP dress, bend radius, service loops) in partnership with optical and network engineers
Experience taking a rack from NPI onto an in-house manufacturing line (fixtures, cycle time, poka-yoke, rework loops)
Thermal and structural analysis (CFD, FEA) used to make a design decision
Time at a high-velocity hardware organization: AI/GPU cloud, custom compute, or an OEM/ODM team that owned the product end to end
Comfort in a factory or datacenter build environment, including first articles, yield, and hardware debug on the floor
